title: Math is Boundless
contentObjective: I can create and describe geometric designs using repetition, patterns, and rhythm, and use a pattern unit to predict what comes next.
languageObjective: I can describe a design using the words repetition, pattern, pattern unit, and rhythm.

turnAndTalk.question: A border repeats pink circle, purple square, blue triangle. Using its pattern unit, how do you predict what shape number 12 is without drawing all 12 shapes?
turnAndTalk.kernel: The pattern unit is 3 shapes long, and 12 ÷ 3 = 4 with no remainder, so shape 12 ends a complete unit — it is the blue triangle.

stems.en: I predict shape 12 by dividing ___ by the ___ length.
stems.es: Predigo la figura 12 al dividir ___ entre la longitud de la ___.

stems.en: Shape 12 is the ___ because the remainder is ___.
stems.es: La figura 12 es el ___ porque el residuo es ___.

turnAndTalk.listenFor: A strong answer divides 12 by 3, gets remainder 0, and explains that means the LAST shape in the unit. A weak answer just guesses the shape without dividing.
turnAndTalk.extend: Using the same pattern, predict shape number 20 — and explain what a remainder of 2 tells you that a remainder of 0 does not.
extendStems: Shape 20 is the ___ because 20 ÷ 3 leaves a remainder of ___.
A remainder of 2 tells me ___, which is different from a remainder of 0 because ___.

turnAndTalk.question: When you sorted design descriptions into 'predictable' and 'rhythm (varies),' what made the circle painting belong with rhythm instead of pattern?
turnAndTalk.kernel: The circle painting's colors, sizes, and ring counts vary with no repeating unit, so it has no predictability the way a pattern does.

stems.en: The circle painting is rhythm because ___.
stems.es: La pintura de círculos es ritmo porque ___.

stems.en: It is not a pattern because it lacks a ___.
stems.es: No es un patrón porque le falta una ___.

turnAndTalk.listenFor: Listen for students naming the missing repeating unit as the reason it's rhythm, not just 'it looks random.'
turnAndTalk.extend: Could a design have BOTH a pattern and rhythm at the same time, in different parts of the same picture? Give an example to defend your answer.
extendStems: Yes/No, because a design could have a pattern in ___ and rhythm in ___.

turnAndTalk.question: The circle-square-triangle border and a tiled wall border both use pattern units. If a tiled wall's unit is 4 tiles long, how would you predict tile number 25?
turnAndTalk.kernel: Dividing the position number by the pattern unit's length, then reading the remainder, tells you which shape in the unit appears at any position — the method works for any unit length.

stems.en: For the tiled wall, I would divide ___ by ___ to find the remainder.
stems.es: Para el muro de azulejos, dividiría ___ entre ___ para hallar el residuo.

stems.en: This is the same method as the border because both use a ___.
stems.es: Este es el mismo método que el borde porque ambos usan una ___.

turnAndTalk.listenFor: A strong answer transfers the divide-and-check-remainder method to a different unit length and correctly computes 25 ÷ 4. A weak answer just says 'do the same thing' without applying it.
turnAndTalk.extend: If tile number 25 in the 4-tile pattern unit design lands on the 1st tile of its unit, what does that tell you about tile number 29? Justify your reasoning.
extendStems: Tile 29 would be the ___ tile in its unit because ___.
I know this because a pattern unit ___.

turnAndTalk.question: During practice, when a problem asked you to predict a shape at a large position number, what strategy helped you find it quickly?
turnAndTalk.kernel: Dividing the position number by the pattern unit's length and reading the remainder tells you exactly which shape appears there.

stems.en: I found the shape by ___ the position number by the unit's ___.
stems.es: Encontré la figura al ___ el número de posición entre la ___ de la unidad.

stems.en: I knew my answer was reasonable because ___.
stems.es: Supe que mi respuesta era razonable porque ___.

turnAndTalk.listenFor: Listen for students naming division and remainder as the specific strategy, not just "I counted it out."
turnAndTalk.extend: How would you help a classmate who forgot that a remainder of 0 means the LAST shape in the unit, not a new one starting? Use one vocabulary word.
extendStems: I would tell them to ___ first because ___.
The mistake happens when you ___ instead of ___.

vocabulary.definition: The same object, shape, or form repeated multiple times.
vocabulary.definitionEs: El mismo objeto, figura o forma repetido varias veces.
vocabulary.example: A row of identical squares across a tiled wall.
vocabulary.visual: The same tile, over and over, all the way along the border.
vocabulary.cloze: The same object or shape repeated multiple times is ___.

examples.text: One shape used again and again, unchanged
The same shape in four different sizes
examples.why: Varying the size makes it rhythm, not repetition.

vocabulary.definition: A set of objects or shapes that are repeated and arranged in a regular order.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Un conjunto de objetos o figuras que se repiten y se organizan en un orden regular.
vocabulary.example: Circle, square, triangle — circle, square, triangle — again and again.
vocabulary.visual: Circle, square, triangle, circle, square, triangle …
vocabulary.cloze: Objects or shapes repeated in a regular order form a ___.

examples.text: 1, 3, 7, 15, 31 — each is double the last plus 1
examples.why: The change follows a rule you can predict.
Nothing lets you say what comes next.

vocabulary.definition: The smallest chunk of a pattern that repeats.
vocabulary.definitionEs: La parte más pequeña de un patrón que se repite.
vocabulary.example: In circle-square-triangle repeated, the pattern unit is those three shapes.
vocabulary.visual: circle · square · triangle — the chunk that starts over.
vocabulary.cloze: The smallest chunk of a pattern that repeats is the ___ ___.

examples.text: The three shapes before the pattern starts again
examples.why: It is the smallest repeating piece.

examples.text: The first six shapes of that pattern
examples.why: That is the unit twice, not the unit.

vocabulary.definition: A design element created by varying the placement, size, orientation, or order of the same objects or shapes.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Un elemento de diseño creado al variar la posición, el tamaño, la orientación o el orden de los mismos objetos o figuras.
vocabulary.example: Circles of different sizes and colors scattered with a flow, like in a painting.
vocabulary.visual: The same circles, but sizes and spacing change as your eye travels.
vocabulary.cloze: Varying the placement, size, or order of the same shapes creates ___.

examples.text: Circles that grow and shift along a row
examples.why: Same objects, varied appearance — flow without predictability.
Nothing varies, so that is a pattern.

vocabulary.definition: Being able to know what comes next because the design follows a rule.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Poder saber qué viene después porque el diseño sigue una regla.
vocabulary.example: Repetition and patterns have it; rhythm often lacks it.
vocabulary.visual: Shape 25 must be a circle — the unit repeats every 3.
vocabulary.cloze: Knowing what comes next because the design follows a rule is ___.

examples.why: The rule tells you before you look.

examples.text: Guessing the next shape in a rhythm design
examples.why: Rhythm varies on purpose, so it often cannot be predicted.

launch.narrative: Geometry is an integral part of design. Geometric patterns have been used to decorate homes and buildings for centuries — in art, architecture, and clothing. This lesson looks at three elements of geometric design: repetition, pattern, and rhythm.

conceptIntro.heading: Repetition, pattern, and rhythm
conceptIntro.intro: The first element of design is repetition: the same object or shape repeated multiple times. Because it involves one object, it has predictability. The second element is a pattern: a set of objects or shapes repeated and arranged in a regular order.
conceptIntro.keyIdea: Tessellations, Geometry & Mathematical Art. 1. Tessellation: Repeating pattern of polygons covering a plane with zero gaps and no overlaps. 2. Interior angles around every vertex must sum to exactly 360°. 3. Use translations, rotations, and reflections to generate symmetrical tile patterns

iDo.title: Watch me use a pattern unit
lines: A border repeats: pink circle, purple square, blue triangle, pink circle, purple square, blue triangle, ...
The pattern unit is 3 shapes long: circle, square, triangle.
To predict shape number 12, I divide: 12 ÷ 3 = 4 with no remainder, so shape 12 ends a complete unit — it is the blue triangle.
The next three shapes after any complete unit will be a pink circle, a purple square, and a blue triangle.
linesEs: Un borde se repite: círculo rosa, cuadrado morado, triángulo azul, círculo rosa, cuadrado morado, triángulo azul, …
La unidad del patrón mide 3 figuras: círculo, cuadrado, triángulo.
Para predecir la figura número 12, divido: 12 ÷ 3 = 4 sin residuo, así que la figura 12 termina una unidad completa — es el triángulo azul.
Las tres figuras que siguen después de cualquier unidad completa serán un círculo rosa, un cuadrado morado y un triángulo azul.
iDo.titleEs: Mírame usar una unidad de patrón

weDo.title: Let's predict shape number 20 together
lines: The pattern unit is still 3 shapes long.
20 ÷ 3 = 6 complete units with a remainder of 2, because 6 × 3 = 18 and 20 − 18 = 2.
A remainder of 2 means shape 20 is the second shape in the unit.
The second shape is the purple square.
linesEs: La unidad del patrón sigue midiendo 3 figuras.
20 ÷ 3 = 6 unidades completas con residuo de 2, porque 6 × 3 = 18 y 20 − 18 = 2.
Un residuo de 2 significa que la figura 20 es la segunda figura de la unidad.
La segunda figura es el cuadrado morado.

youDo.title: Now you try
lines: Draw a pattern with a pattern unit of your own — at least 3 shapes long.
Trade with a partner and predict each other's 15th shape. Check by counting.
linesEs: Dibuja un patrón con una unidad propia — de al menos 3 figuras.
Intercambia con un compañero y predigan la 15.ª figura del otro. Compruébenlo contando.

interactiveVisual.label: Divide by the pattern unit and check the remainder.

conceptIntro.introEs: El primer elemento del diseño es la repetición: el mismo objeto o figura repetido varias veces. Como se trata de un solo objeto, es predecible. El segundo elemento es un patrón: un conjunto de objetos o figuras repetidos y acomodados en un orden regular.
conceptIntro.keyIdeaEs: Teselados, geometría y arte matemático. 1. Teselado: patrón repetido de polígonos que cubre un plano sin huecos ni traslapes. 2. Los ángulos interiores alrededor de cada vértice deben sumar exactamente 360°. 3. Usa traslaciones, rotaciones y reflexiones para generar patrones de mosaicos simétricos

diagram.intro: Drag the point to a position in the repeating design. The distance from zero is the position number. With a pattern unit 4 shapes long, divide: position 7 is 7 ÷ 4 = 1 remainder 3, so position 7 shows the 3rd shape of the unit.

explore.label: Predictable or varied? Sort each design description.

cards.text: The same square tile repeated across a whole wall
Circle, square, triangle repeated in the same order forever
Circles whose colors, sizes, and thickness all vary across the canvas
You can name exactly what the next three shapes will be
The same shapes appear, but their size and order of appearance keep changing
A design with a clear pattern unit that repeats in a regular arrangement
The design has a flow, but you cannot predict what comes next
Concentric circles where the number of rings inside each circle varies

explore.instructions: Repetition and patterns have predictability — you know what comes next. Rhythm uses the same objects but varies their size, orientation, and order, so it often lacks predictability. After sorting, tell a partner which kind of design you find more visually appealing.

connect.scenario: An artist's painting shows rows of circles. The colors and sizes of the circles vary, as does the number of concentric circles within each circle. The painting has rhythm.
connect.promptQuestion: How is a design with rhythm different from a pattern?
connect.prompt: The circle painting's colors and sizes ___, which is why it differs from a ___ — you cannot ___ what the next circle will look like.

check.stem: In the circle painting, the colors, sizes, and ring counts change from circle to circle with no repeating unit. What design element does this describe?
check.explanation: Rhythm is created by varying the placement, size, or order of the same objects. Repetition means one shape repeats exactly, a pattern unit is the repeating chunk of a pattern, and predictability is the trait a pattern has that this painting does not.

check.stem: Why can you NOT predict what the next circle in the painting will look like?
choices: Because rhythm varies color, size, and the number of rings instead of repeating a fixed unit
Because the artist used no shapes at all in the painting
Because the painting contains too many pattern units to count
Because circles are not allowed to be part of a geometric design
check.explanation: A pattern's predictability comes from a repeating unit; rhythm keeps the same object (a circle) but varies how it appears, so there is no fixed unit to predict from.

check.stem: A new row of circles is being added to the painting. Which addition keeps the design consistent with rhythm rather than turning it into a pattern?
choices: New circles with different colors, sizes, and ring counts than any existing row
An exact copy of the very first row, repeated precisely
Circles that follow a strict, repeating 3-shape unit
Replacing all the circles with a single repeated square
check.explanation: Rhythm continues by varying the same object in new ways, not by repeating an existing row exactly — an exact copy or a strict repeating unit would turn the design into a pattern instead.

connect.modelAnswer: The painting demonstrates rhythm because the colors, sizes, and thickness of the circles vary, as does the number of concentric circles inside each one. A pattern would repeat the same unit in a regular order, so I could predict the next circle exactly — with rhythm I cannot. A new row could use the same circles but in different sizes and colors, keeping the flow without copying any existing row.

approaching.stem: In geometric design, what is repetition?
choices: The same object or shape repeated multiple times
A set of different shapes arranged randomly
Shapes that vary in size and order of appearance
approaching.explanation: Repetition involves one repeated object, shape, or form — and because of that, it has predictability.
choiceFeedback: A random arrangement has no rule, so it is neither repetition nor a pattern.
Varying size and order describes rhythm, not repetition.
Color alone does not make a design element — repetition is about a repeated shape.
hints: The word itself is a clue: something repeats.
How many different objects does repetition involve?
One object or shape, repeated multiple times.
approaching.stemEs: En el diseño geométrico, ¿qué es la repetición?
approaching.explanationEs: La repetición usa un objeto, figura o forma repetido — y por eso es predecible.
hintsEs: La palabra misma es una pista: algo se repite.
¿Cuántos objetos distintos usa la repetición?
Un objeto o figura, repetido varias veces.

approaching.stem: A border shows: pink circle, purple square, blue triangle, pink circle, purple square, blue triangle. What are the next three shapes?
choices: Pink circle, purple square, blue triangle
Blue triangle, purple square, pink circle
Pink circle, blue triangle, purple square
approaching.explanation: The pattern unit is circle, square, triangle, so it repeats in the same order: a pink circle, a purple square, and a blue triangle.
choiceFeedback: That reverses the unit — a pattern repeats in the SAME order, not backwards.
That swaps the square and triangle; the unit's order never changes.
A pattern has predictability — that is exactly what makes it a pattern.
hints: Find the chunk that repeats.
The unit is circle, square, triangle.
After a triangle, the unit starts over.
approaching.stemEs: Un borde muestra: círculo rosado, cuadrado morado, triángulo azul, círculo rosado, cuadrado morado, triángulo azul. ¿Cuáles son las siguientes tres figuras?
approaching.explanationEs: La unidad del patrón es círculo, cuadrado, triángulo, así que se repite en el mismo orden: un círculo rosado, un cuadrado morado y un triángulo azul.
hintsEs: Halla el bloque que se repite.
La unidad es círculo, cuadrado, triángulo.
Después de un triángulo, la unidad vuelve a empezar.

approaching.stem: In the circle-square-triangle border, how many shapes long is the pattern unit?
approaching.explanation: The smallest repeating chunk is circle, square, triangle — 3 shapes.
choiceFeedback: 6 shapes is two copies of the unit — the pattern unit is the SMALLEST chunk that repeats.
After 2 shapes (circle, square) the pattern has not started over yet — the triangle is part of the unit.
1 shape would be repetition of a single object, but here three different shapes repeat.
hints: Where does the pattern start over?
List the shapes until you see the first shape again.
Circle, square, triangle — then it restarts.
approaching.stemEs: En el borde círculo-cuadrado-triángulo, ¿de cuántas figuras es la unidad del patrón?
approaching.explanationEs: El bloque repetido más pequeño es círculo, cuadrado, triángulo — 3 figuras.
hintsEs: ¿Dónde vuelve a empezar el patrón?
Enumera las figuras hasta que veas otra vez la primera figura.
Círculo, cuadrado, triángulo — luego vuelve a empezar.

approaching.stem: Where have you seen geometric patterns decorating a building, clothing, or artwork? Describe the design.
approaching.modelAnswer: The floor of our school hallway has a pattern: two gray tiles, then one blue tile, repeated down the whole hall. The pattern unit is 3 tiles, so I can always predict the next tile.
sentenceStems: I have seen a geometric pattern on ___ .
approaching.stemEs: ¿Dónde has visto patrones geométricos decorando un edificio, ropa o una obra de arte? Describe el diseño.

approaching.stem: What is rhythm in geometric design?
choices: The same objects or shapes with varying placement, size, or order of appearance
One shape repeated exactly, over and over
Shapes arranged in a strict, predictable order
A design with no shapes at all
approaching.explanation: Rhythm is created by varying the placement and order of appearance of the same objects or shapes — it gives patterns a flow and often lacks predictability.
choiceFeedback: One shape repeated exactly is repetition, not rhythm.
A strict predictable order describes a pattern; rhythm varies.
Rhythm still uses objects and shapes — it varies how they appear.
hints: Rhythm uses the SAME shapes as a pattern might.
What is different is how they appear.
Their size, placement, and order VARY.
approaching.stemEs: ¿Qué es el ritmo en el diseño geométrico?
approaching.explanationEs: El ritmo se crea variando la posición y el orden de aparición de los mismos objetos o figuras — da fluidez a los patrones y a menudo no es predecible.
hintsEs: El ritmo usa las MISMAS figuras que podría usar un patrón.
Lo que cambia es cómo aparecen.
Su tamaño, posición y orden VARÍAN.

approaching.stem: How would you compare the visual appeal of a design with just repetition and a design with patterns?
approaching.modelAnswer: A design with just repetition is calm but can feel plain, because one shape repeats with no change. A pattern feels more interesting to me because several shapes take turns in a regular order — there is more to look at, but it is still predictable.
sentenceStems: A design with only repetition feels ___ .
A design with patterns feels ___ because ___ .
approaching.stemEs: ¿Cómo compararías el atractivo visual de un diseño con solo repetición y uno con patrones?

approaching.instructions: A shape tessellates when copies of it cover the plane with no gaps and no overlaps. Sort each regular shape.
approaching.instructionsEs: Una figura tesela cuando sus copias cubren el plano sin huecos ni superposiciones. Clasifica cada figura regular.
approaching.label: Sort each shape: can it tessellate by itself?
approaching.labelEs: Clasifica cada figura: ¿puede teselar por sí sola?
hints: Check the angles meeting at one corner point: they must total exactly 360°.
Squares: 4 × 90° = 360° ✓. Pentagons: 3 × 108° = 324° — a gap is left.
hintsEs: Revisa los ángulos que se juntan en un vértice: deben sumar exactamente 360°.
Cuadrados: 4 × 90° = 360° ✓. Pentágonos: 3 × 108° = 324°: queda un hueco.
approaching.explanation: The 360° vertex test decides everything: squares (4 × 90°), triangles (6 × 60°), and hexagons (3 × 120°) each hit 360° exactly, so they tile with no gaps. Pentagon angles (108°) and octagon angles (135°) cannot combine to 360° alone, and circles always leave curved gaps. Beauty here is arithmetic.
approaching.explanationEs: La prueba de los 360° en el vértice lo decide todo: cuadrados (4 × 90°), triángulos (6 × 60°) y hexágonos (3 × 120°) llegan exactamente a 360°, así que cubren sin huecos. Los ángulos del pentágono (108°) y del octágono (135°) no pueden combinarse solos hasta 360°, y los círculos siempre dejan huecos curvos. La belleza aquí es aritmética.

onLevel.stem: The pattern unit circle-square-triangle repeats. What is shape number 12?
onLevel.explanation: 12 ÷ 3 = 4 with no remainder, so shape 12 ends a complete unit — the triangle, which is the last shape of the unit.
choiceFeedback: The circle is position 1 of a unit — that would need a remainder of 1, but 12 ÷ 3 has remainder 0.
The square is position 2 of a unit — that would need a remainder of 2, but 12 ÷ 3 has remainder 0.
It CAN be determined — a pattern's predictability is the point of the pattern unit.
hints: The unit is 3 shapes long. Divide 12 by 3.
12 ÷ 3 = 4 exactly, remainder 0.
No remainder means the LAST shape of the unit.
onLevel.stemEs: La unidad del patrón círculo-cuadrado-triángulo se repite. ¿Cuál es la figura número 12?
onLevel.explanationEs: 12 ÷ 3 = 4 sin residuo, así que la figura 12 termina una unidad completa — el triángulo, que es la última figura de la unidad.
hintsEs: La unidad mide 3 figuras. Divide 12 entre 3.
12 ÷ 3 = 4 exactamente, residuo 0.
Sin residuo significa la ÚLTIMA figura de la unidad.

onLevel.stem: Same pattern. What is shape number 20?
choices: The 20th shape starts a new pattern
onLevel.explanation: 20 ÷ 3 = 6 remainder 2 (since 6 × 3 = 18 and 20 − 18 = 2), and the second shape in the unit is the purple square.
choiceFeedback: The circle needs a remainder of 1, but 20 − 18 = 2.
The triangle needs a remainder of 0, but 20 ÷ 3 leaves a remainder of 2.
The pattern never changes its unit — position 20 is still inside the same repeating pattern.
hints: How many complete units of 3 fit in 20?
6 units use 18 shapes; 20 − 18 = 2 left over.
Count 2 into the unit: circle, then ___ .
onLevel.stemEs: El mismo patrón. ¿Cuál es la figura número 20?
onLevel.explanationEs: 20 ÷ 3 = 6 con residuo 2 (porque 6 × 3 = 18 y 20 − 18 = 2), y la segunda figura de la unidad es el cuadrado morado.
hintsEs: ¿Cuántas unidades completas de 3 caben en 20?
6 unidades usan 18 figuras; 20 − 18 = 2 sobrantes.
Cuenta 2 dentro de la unidad: círculo, luego ___ .

onLevel.stem: How many COMPLETE pattern units appear in the first 18 shapes of the circle-square-triangle border?
onLevel.explanation: Each unit is 3 shapes, and 18 ÷ 3 = 6 complete units.
choiceFeedback: That subtracts 18 − 3 instead of dividing.
That divides 18 by 2, but the unit has 3 shapes, not 2.
3 is the size of one unit, not the number of units in 18 shapes.
hints: One unit uses 3 shapes.
How many groups of 3 are in 18?
Divide 18 by 3.
onLevel.stemEs: ¿Cuántas unidades COMPLETAS del patrón aparecen en las primeras 18 figuras del borde círculo-cuadrado-triángulo?
onLevel.explanationEs: Cada unidad tiene 3 figuras, y 18 ÷ 3 = 6 unidades completas.
hintsEs: Una unidad usa 3 figuras.
¿Cuántos grupos de 3 hay en 18?
Divide 18 entre 3.

onLevel.stem: A painting shows circles whose colors, sizes, and thickness vary, along with the number of concentric circles inside each one. Describe how the painting demonstrates rhythm.
onLevel.modelAnswer: The painting demonstrates rhythm because it uses the same object — a circle — but everything about how the circles appear varies: their colors, their sizes, their thickness, and how many rings sit inside each one. There is a flow, but no repeating unit you could use to predict the next circle.
sentenceStems: The painting uses the same object, but varies ___ .
It is rhythm and not a pattern because ___ .
onLevel.stemEs: Una pintura muestra círculos cuyos colores, tamaños y grosores varían, junto con el número de círculos concéntricos dentro de cada uno. Describe cómo la pintura demuestra ritmo.

onLevel.stem: How is a design with rhythm different from a pattern?
choices: Rhythm varies size, orientation, and order, so it often lacks predictability; a pattern repeats in a regular order
Rhythm uses shapes and a pattern does not
A pattern varies its shapes and rhythm never does
There is no difference between them
onLevel.explanation: A pattern repeats its unit in a regular arrangement, so it is predictable. Rhythm keeps the same objects but varies how they appear, giving flow without predictability.
choiceFeedback: Both use objects and shapes — the difference is in how they are arranged.
That is backwards: the PATTERN is the regular, predictable one, and rhythm is the one that varies.
They differ in exactly one important way: predictability.
hints: Think about predicting the next shape in each.
In which one can you always predict it?
A pattern is predictable; rhythm often is not.
onLevel.stemEs: ¿En qué se diferencia un diseño con ritmo de un patrón?
onLevel.explanationEs: Un patrón repite su unidad en un arreglo regular, así que es predecible. El ritmo mantiene los mismos objetos pero varía cómo aparecen, dando fluidez sin ser predecible.
hintsEs: Piensa en predecir la siguiente figura en cada uno.
¿En cuál de ellos siempre puedes predecirlo?
Un patrón es predecible; el ritmo a menudo no lo es.

onLevel.stem: If a new row of circles were added to the rhythm painting, what would they look like? Explain your thinking.
onLevel.modelAnswer: The new circles would still be circles, but their colors and sizes would vary and each would hold a different number of concentric rings — maybe a huge pale circle with many thin rings next to a small dark one with two thick rings. I cannot copy an existing row, because rhythm varies instead of repeating.
sentenceStems: The new row would keep ___ but vary ___ .
onLevel.stemEs: Si se agregara una nueva fila de círculos a la pintura de ritmo, ¿cómo se verían? Explica tu razonamiento.

onLevel.label: The border pattern repeats circle, square, triangle. Name the shape at each position.
onLevel.labelEs: El patrón del borde repite círculo, cuadrado, triángulo. Nombra la figura en cada posición.
hints: The pattern unit has 3 shapes — divide the position by 3 and look at the remainder.
Remainder 1 → circle, remainder 2 → square, remainder 0 → triangle.
hintsEs: La unidad del patrón tiene 3 figuras: divide la posición entre 3 y mira el residuo.
Residuo 1 → círculo, residuo 2 → cuadrado, residuo 0 → triángulo.
onLevel.explanation: Division by the pattern unit predicts any position without drawing: 7 ÷ 3 leaves remainder 1 (circle), 12 divides exactly so it closes a unit (triangle), and 20 leaves remainder 2 (square). The remainder — not the drawing — is the prediction tool, which is how a pattern unit gives you shape 25 or shape 1,000 equally fast.
onLevel.explanationEs: La división por la unidad del patrón predice cualquier posición sin dibujar: 7 ÷ 3 deja residuo 1 (círculo), 12 divide exacto y cierra una unidad (triángulo) y 20 deja residuo 2 (cuadrado). El residuo — no el dibujo — es la herramienta de predicción, y así una unidad de patrón te da la figura 25 o la 1,000 con la misma rapidez.

extending.stem: The circle-square-triangle pattern continues. What is shape number 25?
extending.explanation: 25 ÷ 3 = 8 remainder 1 (since 8 × 3 = 24 and 25 − 24 = 1), and the first shape of the unit is the pink circle.
choiceFeedback: The square needs a remainder of 2, but 25 − 24 = 1.
The triangle needs a remainder of 0, but 25 ÷ 3 leaves a remainder of 1.
A pattern is boundless — it continues, so shape 25 exists and is predictable.
hints: How many complete units of 3 fit in 25?
8 units use 24 shapes; 25 − 24 = 1 left over.
A remainder of 1 means the FIRST shape of the unit.
extending.stemEs: El patrón círculo-cuadrado-triángulo continúa. ¿Cuál es la figura número 25?
extending.explanationEs: 25 ÷ 3 = 8 con residuo 1 (porque 8 × 3 = 24 y 25 − 24 = 1), y la primera figura de la unidad es el círculo rosado.
hintsEs: ¿Cuántas unidades completas de 3 caben en 25?
8 unidades usan 24 figuras; 25 − 24 = 1 sobrante.
Un residuo de 1 significa la PRIMERA figura de la unidad.

extending.stem: Which element of geometric design often LACKS predictability?
extending.explanation: Rhythm varies the size, orientation, and order of appearance of the same objects, so it gives flow but often lacks predictability.
choiceFeedback: Repetition is the MOST predictable element — one shape repeats exactly.
A pattern repeats its unit in a regular order, which is what makes it predictable.
The pattern unit is the source of a pattern's predictability, not something that lacks it.
hints: Which element varies size, orientation, and order?
Repetition and patterns both follow strict rules.
The one that varies is the unpredictable one.
extending.stemEs: ¿Cuál elemento del diseño geométrico a menudo NO es predecible?
extending.explanationEs: El ritmo varía el tamaño, la orientación y el orden de aparición de los mismos objetos, así que da fluidez pero a menudo no es predecible.
hintsEs: ¿Cuál elemento varía el tamaño, la orientación y el orden?
La repetición y los patrones siguen reglas estrictas.
El que varía es el impredecible.

extending.stem: Create a design that has repetition, pattern, AND rhythm. Describe (or sketch) it, and label where each element appears.
extending.modelAnswer: My design is a picture frame. The outer border is repetition: one gold square repeated all the way around. The inner border is a pattern: star, moon, star, moon in a regular order, so its pattern unit is 2 shapes. The center has rhythm: the same star shape scattered across the middle in different sizes, angles, and colors, so it flows but cannot be predicted.
sentenceStems: My pattern's unit is ___ , and my rhythm varies ___ .
extending.stemEs: Crea un diseño que tenga repetición, patrón Y ritmo. Descríbelo (o dibújalo) y señala dónde aparece cada elemento.

extending.stem: Why do you think the lesson is called 'Math is Boundless'? Use repetition, pattern, and rhythm in your answer.
extending.modelAnswer: A pattern unit can repeat forever — there is no last circle, square, or triangle, so the design has no boundary. Repetition can cover any wall, patterns let us predict shape 25 or shape 25,000, and rhythm shows that even without predictability, math ideas keep creating endless new designs. The designs, like math, never have to end.
sentenceStems: Rhythm shows math is boundless because ___ .
extending.stemEs: ¿Por qué crees que la lección se llama 'Las matemáticas no tienen límites'? Usa repetición, patrón y ritmo en tu respuesta.

extending.label: Match each vertex arrangement to its angle sum — and what it means for tessellation.
extending.labelEs: Empareja cada arreglo de vértice con su suma de ángulos y lo que significa para la teselación.
hints: Multiply the number of shapes by one interior angle.
Only a sum of exactly 360° closes the vertex — less leaves a gap, more forces an overlap.
hintsEs: Multiplica el número de figuras por un ángulo interior.
Solo una suma de exactamente 360° cierra el vértice: menos deja un hueco, más obliga a superponer.
extending.explanation: Each arrangement is a one-line computation: squares, triangles, and hexagons close the vertex at exactly 360°, which is why they are the only regular polygons that tessellate alone. Pentagons stall at 324°, leaving a 36° gap no pentagon can fill — the same 360° rule behind every honeycomb and tiled floor.
extending.explanationEs: Cada arreglo es un cálculo de una línea: cuadrados, triángulos y hexágonos cierran el vértice exactamente en 360°, y por eso son los únicos polígonos regulares que teselan solos. Los pentágonos se quedan en 324°, dejando un hueco de 36° que ningún pentágono puede llenar: la misma regla de 360° detrás de cada panal y cada piso de mosaicos.

practice.commonMistake: Calling every repeated design a 'pattern.' One identical shape repeated is repetition; a pattern needs a unit of shapes repeating in a regular order; and rhythm varies the shapes' size and order, so it is neither.

diagram.title: Complete Pattern Units in the Border
diagram.caption: The pattern unit is 3 shapes long, so divide the position by 3: 12 ÷ 3 = 4, 18 ÷ 3 = 6, 20 ÷ 3 = 6 remainder 2, 25 ÷ 3 = 8 remainder 1. The quotient counts complete units; the remainder names the shape.

exitTicket.stem: Which statement best matches this lesson's summary of 'Math is Boundless'?
choices: Math can be used to create beautiful designs, which often have repetition, patterns, and rhythm
Designs only count as mathematical if they are perfectly predictable
Rhythm is the only real element of design
exitTicket.explanation: The summary names all three elements — repetition, patterns, and rhythm — as the ways math creates beautiful, endless designs.
hints: Look back at the Summarize slide.
It names three elements of design.
Which option includes all three?
exitTicket.stemEs: ¿Qué afirmación corresponde mejor al resumen de esta lección sobre «las matemáticas no tienen límites»?
choicesEs: Las matemáticas se pueden usar para crear diseños hermosos, que muchas veces tienen repetición, patrones y ritmo
Los diseños solo cuentan como matemáticos si son perfectamente predecibles
El ritmo es el único elemento real del diseño
Los patrones geométricos se inventaron hace poco
exitTicket.explanationEs: El resumen nombra los tres elementos — repetición, patrones y ritmo — como las maneras en que las matemáticas crean diseños hermosos y sin fin.
hintsEs: Vuelve a mirar la diapositiva de resumen.
Nombra tres elementos del diseño.
¿Qué opción incluye las tres?

questions.stem: A bicycle has a gear ratio of 3:1. For each turn of the pedals, the rear wheel turns…
questions.explanation: A 3:1 ratio means 3 wheel rotations for every 1 pedal rotation.
questions.stemEs: Una bicicleta tiene una razón de engranaje de 3:1. Por cada vuelta de los pedales, la rueda trasera gira…
questions.explanationEs: Una razón de 3:1 significa 3 vueltas de rueda por cada 1 vuelta de pedal.

questions.explanation: Multiply both parts by the same number: 2 × 4 = 8 and 3 × 4 = 12. 3:2 reverses the order.
questions.explanationEs: Multiplica las dos partes por el mismo número: 2 × 4 = 8 y 3 × 4 = 12. La 3:2 invierte el orden.

questions.stem: Two wheels turn the same number of times, but one has a larger diameter. The larger wheel…
questions.explanation: A larger wheel covers more ground in one rotation, so it travels farther for the same number of turns.
questions.stemEs: Dos ruedas giran el mismo número de veces, pero una tiene mayor diámetro. La rueda más grande…
questions.explanationEs: Una rueda más grande cubre más terreno en una vuelta, así que recorre más distancia con el mismo número de vueltas.

questions.stem: With a gear ratio of 4:1, how many rear-wheel rotations come from 5 pedal rotations?
questions.explanation: Each pedal turn gives 4 wheel turns, so 5 × 4 = 20. Adding gives 9.
questions.stemEs: Con una razón de engranaje de 4:1, ¿cuántas vueltas de la rueda trasera dan 5 vueltas de pedal?
questions.explanationEs: Cada vuelta de pedal da 4 vueltas de rueda, así que 5 × 4 = 20. Sumar da 9.
